limitations.text: For this build InferRoute recomputed RTMR1+RTMR2+RTMR3 on its own machine from artifacts the operator publishes, and they matched. The root-filesystem measurement — the operating system's programs, libraries and configuration — was recomputed from the file list the operator bakes into the initial RAM filesystem, which the earlier measurement already pins; the files themselves were not rebuilt from source, so their hashes are the operator's output, checked for consistency rather than reproduced.

Whether the AI machine keeps your text after answering it is the operator's claim, not something this computer can check. The copy that lasts is the record on this computer. What the hardware DOES prove is that your words reach a genuine, non-debuggable enclave and are readable nowhere else in transit.

Why this computer cannot check it: InferRoute records the enclave builds it has seen and refuses unrecorded ones, and recomputes what it can — stated per session above. The measurements cover the machine's firmware, its start-up and, in the builds InferRoute accepts, the operating system's programs, libraries and configuration. They do NOT cover what the machine loads after it starts: the software containers the model runs in, which the operator checks against its own signatures rather than measures, and the code the model is served with, which nothing measures — the operator has confirmed that gap and plans to add a proof of it. That software could change without changing any measurement.

The GPU reports are signed by the same quote-bound key as the rest of the evidence, so the enclave itself vouches that these are its GPUs — but NVIDIA provides no way to prove from the outside that an attested GPU is attached to an attested CPU enclave. That step rests on the enclave's measured software, like everything else inside it. NVIDIA also does not report a GPU's confidential-computing mode, so it cannot be checked here.
Your account, session, the model, message sizes and timing are visible to relays; the words are not.
